cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, has set the temple in order. Friend, I've got ONE little bakery and I STILL can't find my spatula. After all this, Neco, king of Egypt, marches up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates.

cards.question: Neco king of Egypt is on the march to Carchemish. What does King Josiah do?

answers.text: He goes out to confront Neco
He sends Neco a gift of gold
He stays in Jerusalem to pray

cards.text: Neco sends messengers to Josiah, and the first thing they say is, “What is the issue between you and me, O king of Judah?” That's the king of EGYPT sounding like a guy you just cut off in traffic.

cards.question: Neco's message tells Josiah that Neco has not come against him today.
Neco says he's fighting another dynasty, and ___ has told him to hurry.

cards.text: Then Neco ends with a warning: “So stop opposing God, who is with me, or He will destroy you!” Friend, that is NOT a message you leave on read.

cards.question: Josiah doesn't turn away from Neco. Instead, to fight him in battle, Josiah ___ himself.
Josiah won't listen to Neco's warning. But whose mouth did those words really come from?
Josiah goes to fight Neco anyway. Where does the battle happen?

cards.text: Josiah heads onto the Plain of Megiddo in disguise, which I respect, because NO disguise on earth could hide this mustache. Then the archers shoot King Josiah.

cards.question: After the archers shoot him, Josiah tells his servants to keep fighting without him.

cards.text: Josiah says, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded!” His servants take him out of his chariot and put him in his second chariot.

cards.question: Josiah's servants bring him to ___, and that's where he dies.

cards.text: Josiah is buried in the tomb of his fathers. The king who set the temple in order is gone.

cards.question: After King Josiah dies, only his servants mourn for him.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah, the prophet, laments over Josiah. And to this day, the male and female singers still recite laments over him.

cards.question: The singers' laments over Josiah become what for Israel?
Those songs the singers recite for Josiah? They get written down in the Book of ___.

cards.text: The rest of Josiah's acts, from beginning to end, and his deeds of loving devotion according to the Law of the LORD? Friend, somebody wrote ALL of it down.

cards.question: The rest of Josiah's acts are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

findings.problem: Only about half the choice cards can be reasoned out from earlier cards. Six of the twelve are pure discovery. Card 2 (Josiah goes out to confront Neco) has no setup that points away from sending gold or staying to pray. Card 5 (God told Neco to hurry) comes before any card mentions God's part. Card 7 (disguised) and card 9 (Plain of Megiddo) have no setup. Card 17 (a statute) has no setup either. Card 20 (the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah) is a coin flip on the book's name. The story cards need more context, or some of these questions should change, so that most choice cards are informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card calls Jeremiah "the prophet." 2 Chronicles 35:25 does not say this, and the card gives no reference for it. The card's only citation is 2 Chronicles 35:25.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: In 2 Chronicles 35:25, "to this day" means the Chronicler's own day. Papa Dorin retells it in his present-tense voice: "And to this day, the male and female singers still recite laments over him." Adding "still" makes it read as if singers recite these laments today. The text does not say that. The retelling also drops "all."
findings.question: When Papa Dorin retells a narrator's "to this day" in his own words, should he keep it tied to the writer's time, for example "in the writer's day," or quote it exactly? Or may he say it in his own present-tense voice?

findings.problem: Card 19 ends with "Friend, somebody wrote ALL of it down." Card 20 is a true or false question about whether Josiah's acts are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. Telling the baker beforehand that his acts were written down pushes them toward True. It gives away most of the answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
